I decided to plant some seeds, put them in potting soil, and they sprouted. Yet, now there is a bunch of these little gnats flying around. One of my plants died, is this because of them? Where did they come from and how do I get rid of them? I tried the drop of soap in apple vinager and just plain water, but they just seem to be multiplying. Any suggestions?
There looks to be tiny white ones crawling in the soil, but the ones that fly are black.

It could be mealy bugs. They can live in the soil as well as on your plant. They tend to live in a symbiotic association with ants.

A good mulching can help control their numbers.

Neem oil and water ( I forget the concentration) disrupts the reproductive cycles of many insects and can be applied to the soil and the plant without harm to plant (or you). Adding soap can burn some plants.

Long term, your plants might need some companions with repellant properties like marigolds or tansys. Rosmary is also good pest repellant.

Sounds like fungus gnats. Go get some GnatNix, yellow sticky traps and a bottle of 3% Hydrogen Peroxide. Mix the Hydrogen Peroxide with water - 1 part per 4 parts of water - and water each effected pot with it. This kills larvae on contact, while providing increased oxygen to the roots.

Next, let your topsoil dry out very well. Once it's good and dry, shop-vac the top inch of soil out of each pot. Now fill the pot back up with your GnatNix and stake your sticky traps in the soil/close to plants without touching any leaves.

These methods always work very well for me. Good luck!
